title: Console: Shadow Evals dashboard MVP (charts, filters, beta flag wiring)
author: Dylan Brooks
release_notes: Adds (beta-flagged) Shadow Evals dashboard MVP in Console with basic time-series + breakdown charts, filters, and deep links. No change to default customer experience unless enabled via feature flag.
body:
Summary: Implements the Console UI MVP for the new Shadow Evals dashboard. This includes: (1) a new Shadow Evals section under Observability for a selected route, (2) time-series charts for key shadow_eval signals (judge win-rate, format adherence, safety outcomes, latency delta, cost delta, shadow error/drop counts), (3) breakdown tables (by shadow target and region) with sortable columns, (4) filter controls (time window, route, region, primary model, shadow target, outcome metric), (5) URL query param sync for shareable links, and (6) wiring behind the beta feature flag so the UI only renders for enabled workspaces.

Context: This PR is the UI half of the MVP paired with the Console backend APIs from PR-48320 and the telemetry emission work from PR-48261. The goal is to let beta customers compare candidate shadow targets against the primary without impacting end-user responses, and give PM/SRE a single place to inspect health + quality signals.

User-visible behavior: Hidden by default. The entire nav entry + pages are behind the feature flag `shadow_evals_dashboard_mvp`. If the flag is off, the route details page does not show the Shadow Evals tab and no shadow metrics queries are made.

What’s included (MVP scope): - New route details tab: `/console/observability/routes/:routeId/shadow-evals` - Global guard: workspace feature flag + permission check (must have access to the route + metrics). - Charts: Judge win-rate (shadow vs primary), Format adherence rate, Safety pass rate, Shadow vs primary p50/p95 latency delta, Estimated token cost delta, Shadow runner drops and errors. - Breakdowns: A) by `shadow_target` (normalized display name), B) by region. - Filters: time window (1h/6h/24h/7d), region (single-select), shadow target (multi-select), outcome metric selector. - Empty states: no data, flag disabled, insufficient permissions, backend not ready (404/501). - Basic client-side bucketing for display (mirrors backend guardrails): collapses high-cardinality values into `Other` and caps breakdown rows at 25 with “show more” disabled for MVP.

Not included / follow-ups: - Export to CSV (planned), - Per-customer allowlist UI (policy lives elsewhere), - “Compare two shadow targets” diff view, - Saved views, - Alert configuration from UI (links to Grafana/alerts for now).

Design notes: Copy and layout follow the DES-147 direction: use “Shadow Evals” terminology (not “shadow traffic”) for customer-facing surfaces; keep the framing comparative (“primary vs shadow”) and emphasize that results do not impact end-user responses.

Screenshots (internal): - Route details > Shadow Evals tab: https://console-dev.redwood.example/screens/48333/route-shadow-evals-overview - Breakdown + filter state: https://console-dev.redwood.example/screens/48333/route-shadow-evals-breakdown

Testing: - Added unit tests for query param sync + filter state reducer. - Added simple rendering tests for the disabled/empty/error states. - Manual: verified with dev backend stub + staging API against a beta workspace with `shadow_evals_dashboard_mvp` enabled.

Rollout: Beta only. This is safe to land because it’s gated and uses existing metrics endpoints. If backend endpoints are absent, UI shows the “Shadow Evals not available” empty state and logs a non-fatal console error with request id.

Risk/mitigations: - Risk: accidentally querying metrics for all users -> mitigated by early feature-flag guard and no background prefetch. - Risk: slow breakdown queries -> mitigated by debounced filter changes and hard cap on breakdown rows (25). - Risk: confusion about SLO impact -> mitigated by banner copy that explicitly states shadow runs do not impact primary response and “Shadow failures do not count against primary SLOs.”
commits: console/ui: add Shadow Evals route tab + page scaffold
console/ui: implement time-series panels for shadow_eval metrics
console/ui: add breakdown tables + sorting + capped row rendering
console/ui: add filters + query param sync + debounce
console/ui: wire workspace feature flag shadow_evals_dashboard_mvp
console/ui: tests for filter reducer and URL sync
review_conversation:
Kenji Nakamura (requested changes): The overall IA matches the mock, but the filter bar spacing is tight and the empty-state copy should avoid implying we store prompts/outputs. Can we say “aggregated metrics only” and link to the beta doc? Also, can the “Shadow target” control show the customer-facing label (model + quant profile) rather than the raw id?

Dylan Brooks (author): Updated filter layout (2-row responsive at <1200px). Adjusted copy to “Aggregated evaluation metrics” and added link to internal doc page. For labels: the API returns `target_display_name`; we now prefer it and fall back to id if missing.

Chloe Martin: Please ensure we don’t hammer the metrics endpoint on every keystroke when changing multi-select. Also verify the UI handles 404 from shadow endpoints gracefully (some workspaces won’t have the pipeline yet).

Dylan Brooks: Added 400ms debounce on filter changes + request cancelation on in-flight queries. Added 404/501 handling with the “not available” empty state.

Logan Wright: Breakdown table needs to respect the cardinality guardrails from the schema doc. We should cap rows and bucket unknowns; also, avoid rendering raw `request_route` if present in payload.

Dylan Brooks: Implemented capped breakdown rows at 25 + `Other` bucket. UI only uses normalized route display name from Console metadata and doesn’t render `request_route`.

Allison Grant: Please add a small help tooltip clarifying that shadow errors/drops are shadow-path only and not primary failures. Also ensure we’re using the standardized metric names (shadow_eval.*) consistently.

Dylan Brooks: Added tooltip next to “Drops/Errors” chart and verified all queries are under shadow_eval.* namespaces.

Marissa Cole (approval): Looks good for beta. Thanks for making URL deep links work—this will help support and success. Please file a follow-up for CSV export and saved views.

Dylan Brooks: Follow-up created in Linear (not blocking this PR).
